facts.headline: The tower everyone calls "Big Ben" isn't actually named that
facts.hook: Big Ben is actually the nickname of the 13.5-tonne bell inside — the tower itself was only officially renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012.

facts.headline: Legend says the kingdom falls the day these six birds leave
facts.hook: Since Charles II's reign, the Tower of London has kept six ravens with clipped wings, guarding a legend that the Crown falls the day they leave.

facts.headline: Buckingham Palace has more rooms than most hotels
facts.hook: Buckingham Palace contains 775 rooms in total — including 92 offices, 78 bathrooms, and 188 staff bedrooms.

facts.headline: The world's first underground railway opened here in 1863
facts.hook: The Metropolitan Railway between Paddington and Farringdon became the world's first underground passenger railway, running steam trains through smoke-filled tunnels in 1863.

facts.headline: A Victorian time capsule has sat buried under this obelisk since 1878
facts.hook: Buried beneath this obelisk since 1878 sits a sealed time capsule packed with cigars, a baby's bottle, and photos of a dozen Victorian women.

facts.headline: A tiny park hides ceramic tributes to strangers who died saving strangers
facts.hook: Postman's Park hides dozens of Victorian ceramic tablets, each honoring an ordinary Londoner who died saving someone else's life.

facts.headline: Knights Templar effigies still lie inside this 800-year-old church
facts.hook: Built by the Knights Templar in the 12th century, Temple Church still holds stone knight effigies — and inspired a key scene in The Da Vinci Code.
